review_notes: Read the whole file. It has no @[simp] attributes of its own. I checked the uses of fracCurve_def, c_eq_algebraMap and thetaPoint_eq_some in the repo (including Scheme/Addition/FormalPoint.lean, where fracCurve_def is used only with rw). The only real simp-interface weakness I found is the lack of coefficient lemmas for fracCurve, which leaves the call sites with ad hoc unfolding. I could not run Lean, so how the proposed lemmas would behave inside simp is untested. Other rfl-lemmas such as thetaPoint_eq_some are deliberately non-simp, since they take a Nonsingular proof argument. I found no cycles or competing rules.

findings.declaration: WeierstrassCurve.fracCurve / fracCurve_def (coefficient reads in thetaPoint_add, thetaPoint_neg)
findings.problem: `fracCurve` has no coefficient lemmas such as `(fracCurve W σ KK).a₁ = algebraMap (MvPowerSeries σ O) KK (C W.a₁)`. Call sites handle this in three different ways. Line 350 unfolds the definition with `simp [fracCurve, c_eq_algebraMap]`. Line 134 uses the provided `fracCurve_def`. Lines 393 and 435 use `simp only [..., c_eq_algebraMap] at h; exact h`, which only works because the resulting form is defeq to `(fracCurve ..).a₁` (not tested). The `c_eq_algebraMap` rewrite points from `C` to `algebraMap`, while `fracCurve_def` goes through `map_a₁` and `RingHom.comp_apply`. So the normal form of a `fracCurve` coefficient is not canonical, and each use has to be tuned to it.
findings.proposed_change: Add coefficient lemmas for `fracCurve`, one each for `a₁ … a₆`. Each would read `(fracCurve W σ KK).aᵢ = algebraMap (MvPowerSeries σ O) KK (C W.aᵢ)`. They could instead be stated with the composite `algebraMap`, whichever form matches `MvPowerSeries.c_eq_algebraMap` consistently. Mark them `@[simp]` if `fracCurve` should stay opaque, or `private` simp lemmas if not. Then replace the `simpa [fracCurve, …]` and `simp only [..., c_eq_algebraMap] at h; exact h` blocks (lines 350, 356, 393, 435) by `simpa [fracCurve_a₁, …] using h`, so `fracCurve` is never unfolded.
findings.benefit: The same form of a `fracCurve` coefficient is produced and consumed everywhere. The proofs no longer depend on accidental defeq closing `exact h`, and they no longer unfold `fracCurve` in some places and not in others. The repeated blocks in `thetaPoint_add` and `thetaPoint_neg` become short `simp` calls.

evidence.excerpt: simp only [map_sub, map_mul, map_one, MvPowerSeries.c_eq_algebraMap] at h
